title: Sickle Cell Disease
result: Expert-authored, peer-reviewed chapter, first posted 15 September 2003, comprehensive update 17 November 2022, revised 13 February 2025. Sickle haemoglobin (HbS) results from HBB c.20A>T, p.Glu6Val in the hemoglobin convention that starts numbering after the initiator methionine (p.Glu7Val in standard HGVS numbering). Sickle cell disease is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner; Hb S/S is the most common form. In deoxygenated HbS, an interaction between Val6 and complementary regions on adjacent molecules forms highly ordered, insoluble polymers that distort red blood cells; HbS polymerises in the T conformation associated with deoxygenation but not in the R conformation. Heterozygotes (Hb A/S, sickle cell trait) are not anaemic, have normal red cell indices and HbS near 40%, and Hb A/S confers a survival advantage in children who contract malaria.
